setupSteps: Connect an Android phone by authorized USB or Wi-Fi debugging for setup diagnostics, or use an already provisioned Agent Mesh phone path.
Start the provisioned Even companion bridge on the phone or classroom host.
Wear the G2 and confirm that its voice or button interaction appears in Agent Mesh.
Use the Coding agents card's Connect button to attach the shared bridge; this card then reports the G2 independently.
integrations.safetyNote: Only semantic interactions and bounded display text enter the Fabric; raw microphone data is not discovered or recorded.

setupSteps: Connect an Android phone by authorized USB or Wi-Fi debugging for setup diagnostics, or use an already provisioned Agent Mesh phone path.
Start the approved Meta phone bridge and keep the phone on the classroom network.
Wear the glasses and confirm that their semantic interaction appears in Agent Mesh.
Use the Coding agents card's Connect button for agent requests; use the separate media source control when camera streaming is enabled.
integrations.safetyNote: Agent Mesh carries semantic interactions only. Camera media uses the explicit media companion and is never recorded by discovery.

setupSteps: Start Codex or Claude in the approved lesson workspace.
Choose Connect to attach an approved live session.
integrations.safetyNote: Discovery never starts an agent or grants filesystem, shell, or device credentials.

setupSteps: Plug the controller directly into USB and start Ultraleap Tracking.
Choose Connect input after the controller is found.
integrations.safetyNote: The scan does not open the tracking stream and never creates a robot command.

integrations.connectionMethod: Wi-Fi, USB/RNDIS, or DJI app bridge
setupSteps: Power the robot on with its wheels raised for the first test.
Choose STA, AP, RNDIS, or the stock S1 app transport.
Connect while disarmed, then use the lesson controls to arm it.
integrations.safetyNote: A network match is not proof of a robot; only the adapter handshake confirms it, and movement stays disarmed.

setupSteps: Charge BOLT, wake it in its cradle, and keep the displayed SB-XXXX name visible.
Close Sphero Edu, Sphero Play, or another program that is currently connected to this robot.
Choose Find devices. Select the exact SB-XXXX robot when the CIT Sphero adapter is available; never select the nearest anonymous robot.
integrations.safetyNote: Discovery only reads Windows Bluetooth presence. It does not connect, wake, roll, aim, or change LEDs; physical movement still requires a bounded CIT adapter and an armed lesson.

setupSteps: Charge and switch on Dash or Dot, then place it near this Windows computer.
Close Wonder, Blockly, or any other app that is currently connected to the robot.
Choose Find devices, select each exact named Dash or Dot, and choose Connect selected.
Sensor monitoring starts unarmed. Dash movement, head motion, and sound remain locked until a tutor arms the physical lesson.
integrations.safetyNote: Discovery is read-only and never selects the nearest robot. Dash movement is bounded and has a 350 ms local deadman stop; Dot never advertises movement.

setupSteps: Remove propellers for the first connection test and power on each grounded aircraft.
Use one physical USB Wi-Fi adapter per stock Tello, or unique station-mode addresses.
Choose Connect grounded drones, then assign the fleet controller and each input on the integrated page.
Flight remains a separate one-shot arm with four tutor confirmations.
integrations.safetyNote: Discovery and connection send no takeoff or movement command. Aircraft nodes expose telemetry, land, and emergency stop; a separate controller exposes only the bounded ordered sequence.

setupSteps: Pair MindWave Mobile 2 in Windows Bluetooth settings.
Start ThinkGear Connector and select the headset's outgoing COM port.
Choose Connect headset after ThinkGear Connector is ready.
integrations.safetyNote: Only vendor-labelled semantic metrics are surfaced. Raw EEG is neither published nor stored.

setupSteps: Connect exactly one Brain2Devices fleet slot and MindWave from the device cards above.
Assign the bounded demo controller in the Devices, sensors, cameras, and safe demos lesson.
Practice in Simulation first; physical arming requires the on-screen instructor checklist.
integrations.safetyNote: This one-shot workflow is independent from the sensor and drone adapters. It exposes no general takeoff or movement command and cannot be armed by an autonomous agent.

setupSteps: Use a plug whose packaging or label shows the Matter logo and setup code.
Put the plug in pairing mode on the classroom network.
Enter the printed code in Classroom Control; no vendor account is required.
integrations.safetyNote: Commissioning never turns a load on. Connecting places each approved outlet in the off safe state.

setupSteps: Install Pybricks firmware on the supported hub.
Give each classroom hub a unique advertised name and bind that exact name.
Keep motors raised or disconnected for the first framed-protocol test.
integrations.safetyNote: Discovery never chooses the nearest anonymous BLE hub and never arms a motor.
